rationale: Evidence. Iteration 8 (kp 7.0, kd 0.3, outer sensors at x = ±0.06, sensor_size 0.016) scored 62.23, below iteration 6 (kd 0.2, score 64.74). Steering oscillation fell on the oval (0.159 to 0.156) and on the s-bend (0.173 to 0.130), while s-bend progress held at 0.1425 and s-bend max_error stayed at 0.063. The derivative term is damping the bend response without losing s-bend progress. The score drop came from the oval (progress 0.218 to 0.202) and slalom (progress 0.103 to 0.096, line_loss_events 1.0 per run). Slalom is the weakest track and has lost the line once per run in every race. Evaluator branch (a) applies: oscillation is below 0.16 on the oval and s-bend, s-bend progress holds near 0.14, and max_error stays near 0.06 m. So kd 0.3 is kept and the next single-group change is line_loss = search_right, as the Evaluator requested. Geometry (sensors at x = -0.06, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.06 at y = 0.04; sensor_size 0.016; wheel_track 0.12; wheel_radius 0.03; body 0.16 x 0.12; mass 0.7), base_speed 1.4, kp 7.0, ki 0.0 and the sensor weights are unchanged, so the race isolates the line-loss behaviour. Change: line_loss from last_direction to search_right. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall or slalom progress rises above 0.10, with oscillation and s-bend progress roughly unchanged. Risk: search_right steers left on loss, so if the slalom line is lost on a right-hand curve this could worsen the run. Hypotheses: (1) if slalom progress rises and line_loss_events drop, keep search_right. (2) If slalom progress falls or the oval/s-bend change, revert to last_direction and address the slalom loss another way. (3) If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, plus completion_time and rms_error.
